summary.headline: Titagarh Q2 FY27: 51 metro cars invoiced (up from 30 in Q1) and order book of about Rs 28,600-8,700 crore including JV share.
summary.overview: Management said metro car invoicing rose to 51 in Q2 from 30 in Q1, putting the company on pace toward its 200-car annual target. Wagon demand uncertainty eased after receipt of option quantity orders from Indian Railways, and management targets returning to 1,000 wagons per month by FY28. Passenger rail systems now make up about 30%+ of revenue, and passenger rail is nearly 70% of standalone order book. The Vande Bharat JV agreement with BHEL was signed, and the Vande Bharat prototype is expected to be ready for packaging by Q4 FY27. Transcript quality was poor in places (garbled ASR-style text), so some figures and project timelines are approximate.

segments.name: Metro (PRS)
segments.commentary: 51 metro cars invoiced in Q2 vs 30 in Q1; management aims for close to 200 cars in FY27 and projects about 275 cars in FY28 across projects. Bangalore metro expected to complete this year; Surat and Andhra trains partly delivered.

segments.name: Main line / Vande Bharat (PRS)
segments.commentary: Prototype train production in full swing with first train expected ready for packaging by Q4 FY27. Contract is 1,288 cars plus 30% option; management projects about 192 coaches by FY28 per analyst's reading of guidance. Vande Bharat propulsion supplied by BHEL under consortium.

segments.name: Wagons (Trade)
segments.commentary: Option quantity orders received from Indian Railways give near-term visibility. Target to return to 1,000 wagons per month by FY28; in the past year management said 100 cars target delivered only 63 (context on wagons/cars mixed in transcript).

segments.name: Aluminium metro coaches (Pune)
segments.commentary: First fully India-made aluminium car expected June-July 2026 (FY28 per transcript); first Pune train delivery planned Q3/Q4 FY28.

guidance_outlook: Metro: aim for close to 200 cars in FY27 (51 invoiced in Q2, 30 in Q1).
Wagons: target return to 1,000 wagons per month by FY28, backed by option orders; long-term Railways market-share and logistics-cost plans described as unchanged.

Vande Bharat: first prototype expected ready for packaging by Q4 FY27; series production clearance expected after prototype test (about 3 months) and second train; FY28 projection of 192 coaches referenced by analyst.
Mumbai Metro Line 6 prototype expected Q4 FY27 (or Q1 CY2027 per answer); Line 5 prototype to follow immediately.
Capex: management said KPEX for in-house propulsion is largely already invested; no need to raise capex for current propulsion plans.
capex_capacity: Vande Bharat/main line facility is separate from metro line at Uttarpara plant; facility already set up and capable of targeted production.
Aluminium production area under construction; equipment largely acquired to produce flat-pack extrusions in India instead of importing from Hungary-linked partner (as transcribed).
Joint venture with a partner (transcribed as Ramakrishna/Rhamakrishna) to add wheel capacity expected to reduce wheel-supply risk when the next cycle comes.
Propulsion: in-house propulsion planned after ramp-up; partner propulsion (BHEL, ABB, Siemens, NELCO) used in past projects.
demand_pricing: Vande Bharat contracts are largely price-variation contracts; management says direct cost inflation is neutralised, with delays affecting cash flow and overheads.

Management says demand for metro is in pipeline across Bangladesh, Pune, Delhi, Chennai, Nagpur, Ahmedabad, Surat and Patna; management declined to size win probability. Analyst cited Rs 450-500 crore total cost for some of these tenders (analyst's figure).
Management sees high-speed rail (seven corridors) as the next large opportunity, with aluminium coaches as the standard globally; no formal strategy articulated yet.

qa_highlights.question: Are there delays on the Vande Bharat and metro projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adjusted timelines (16 to 24 coaches, spec changes) are acknowledged by customers and projects are on time, with rescheduling and no penalties applied, as is expected for Vande Bharat and Mumbai lines.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in 192 Vande Bharat coaches by FY28 versus metro ramp-up pace; Siemens MOU; propulsion roadmap and KPEX.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main line facility is separate from metro and already capable of target output; contracted test and approval schedule (about 3 months per test cycle) underpins FY28 projection. Siemens MOU is non-binding, non-exclusive, for cost-effective global rolling stock projects. Propulsion to be in-house after ramp-up; KPEX already largely invested.

qa_highlights.question: Mumbai Metro Line 5 and Line 6 status and FY28 deliveries.
qa_highlights.answer: Line 6 prototype expected Q4 FY27 and Line 5 immediately after; car body production started. Supply-chain delays (Gulf war, electronic kits) were allowed by Government of India circular. Management declined project-wise FY28 split; overall FY28 target about 275 cars.

qa_highlights.question: Bangalore, Surat and Andhra metro status; Pune aluminium coach timeline; traction motor supply.
qa_highlights.answer: Bangalore expected to complete this year; a couple of trains already delivered each to Surat and Andhra. First fully India-made aluminium car expected in mid-2026 (transcribed as June/July FY28), Pune first delivery Q3/Q4 FY28. Traction motor number not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Order-flow pipeline for wagons and metro; supply-chain and electronic-component strategy.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wagon demand may be deferred by a few quarters but not extinguished; metro pipeline and line extensions expected to lead to new orders. Supply-chain issues handled case by case (wheels, electronic components, battery issues); some past delivery shortfalls (100 cars target vs 63 delivered).

qa_highlights.question: Vande Bharat prototype delay impact on margin; wagon capacity ramp.
qa_highlights.answer: Vande Bharat delay impacts cash flow and overheads but not margin, since direct costs are under price-variation clauses. Prototype delivery likely late Q4. Wagon ramp to 1,000 per month by FY28 now supported by orders.

risks_watch: Vande Bharat prototype timing (Q4 FY27) and subsequent test/approval cycle before series production clearance.
Supply-chain constraints: electronic components, wheels, battery and Gulf-war-related delays; past shortfall of 100 cars target vs 63 delivered.
Wagon demand timing: management acknowledges demand can be deferred by a few quarters; ramp to 1,000 wagons per month depends on order visibility.
Mumbai Metro Line 5/6 prototype dates and execution timelines not disclosed project-by-project.
Management declined to give project-level detail on tenders, traction motor volumes and execution timelines, limiting visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the overall demand and metro ramp, but evasive on project-level timelines, tender win expectations, traction motor volumes and high-speed strategy. Cautious on supply-chain issues, acknowledging past delivery shortfalls.
